newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Trader purchase holds up diesel.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Trader purchase holds up diesel.

text.p: The soft Singapore gas oil market was propped up on Thursday by active buying by a Japanese trader, while jet fuel was discussed at lower levels amid soft regional demand, traders said.

The trader, Marubeni International Petroleum Co, bought a total of 600,000 barrels of gas oil in four cargoes at between $25.10 and $25.35 per barrel for end-May to mid-June lifting on a free-on-board (fob) basis.
The sellers were a Swiss trader, a Mediterranean trader and another Japanese trader.

Traders were initially concerned that gas oil values would bust below the $25.00-support level for the first time this year after Taiwan sold by tender two cargoes of 0.3-percent sulphur gas oil for June 4-17 lifting to Swiss and German traders.
The awarded level of $24.58 per barrel was deemed very low by state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp.

Traders were mixed on the near term outlook on gas oil. Some pointed out that sustained high stocks of middle-distillates in Singapore would see prices slipping further. Stocks for the week-ended May 14 rose by 166,000 barrels to 8.96 million barrels, the TDB said earlier.
But others said the closed arbitrage from the West would help to limit supplies coming into Asia and curb a freefall.

The current soft gas oil market was also reflected in Sri Lanka's gas oil and jet fuel purchase tenders which received the lowest offer from Vitol of 14 cents per barrel below Singapore quotes and a five-cent discount respectively for early June delivery.
Singapore jet fuel was offered lower at $24.60 and $24.80 per barrel for mid-June lifting with a bid seen at $24.80.

Bangladesh was heard to have awarded its spot tender for May 23-24 lifting at $1.09 per barrel above Singapore spot quotes c-and-f Chittagong. In its last tender Bangladesh bought from Glencore at a $1.48-premium for end-April delivery.
